_comment_syntax_version: v740sp08 is the lowest ABAP release this tool targets, so nothing newer
than 7.40 SP08 may be used. It is a floor, not the release of any one
The pin only has an effect through parser_error and check_syntax.
abaplint runs ONLY the rules that are listed in this file, so both are
listed on purpose: without them, code that is not ABAP at all passes.
_comment_keyword_case: keyword_case is deliberately NOT enabled. Objects are authored through
ADT and SAP's Class Builder regenerates the DEFINITION section of every
global class in its own canonical style on activation, so enforcing a
casing convention on code SAP rewrites only produces churn.
_comment_object_naming: Enforces the naming scheme AND the DDIC length limits in one place:
classes and interfaces at most 30 characters, tables and lock objects
at most 16, programs at most 40. Written with explicit character
classes on purpose: abaplint drops the backslash of \w in these
patterns, which silently turns them into a literal 'w'.
A user-supplied object_naming block REPLACES abaplint's defaults, so
object types that are not listed here (function groups, data elements,
domains, message classes, transactions) are not checked at all. Add a
pattern when the first such object appears.
There is no pattern for the package: abaplint takes the package name
from the file name package.devc.xml, so it always sees 'PACKAGE'.
The package name is checked in review. The tabl pattern also covers
structures, which DDIC would allow up to 30 characters.
_comment_forbidden_identifier: First pattern: the 30-character identifier cap. ABAP rejects a longer
name at compile time, which surfaces as a hard error after a full SAP
round trip, while abaplint is otherwise clean on the same file.
Second pattern: no sy-datum, sy-uzeit, sy-datlo, sy-timlo. Every
timestamp is an explicit UTC TIMESTAMPL. abaplint sees the component
token, not 'sy-datum', so this matches the bare names DATUM, UZEIT,
DATLO and TIMLO anywhere - it also flags an unrelated component of one
of those names. That is a known false positive; give such a component
another name. It cannot check that a timestamp is really a TIMESTAMPL;
that is a review item. Patterns are case-insensitive.
